what: WORKED COMPUTATION (independent run 1 of 2): Can a formation law carry waves? In a linear gain-one formation model the record at level t+1 is a POSITIVE-weight average of records at earlier levels: theta_{t+1} = sum_{j>=0} sum_p w_{j,p} theta_{t-j}(x+p) + noise, w >= 0, sum w = 1. (1) For one level of memory (j = 0): the mode multiplier is phi(k), |phi| <= 1, and 1 - |phi| = O(k^2): diffusive. (2) For two levels (j = 0, 1) with weights a and 1 - a: solve lambda^2 - a phi(k) lambda - (1-a) psi(k) = 0 for symmetric sets; compute |lambda(k)| at small k for a in {0.25, 0.5, 0.75} and several predecessor sets: is there ANY positive-weight choice with |lambda(k)| = 1 - O(k^4) and arg lambda = c|k| (a propagating wave)? (3) Prove or find numerically the obstruction: with positive weights the root near 1 satisfies lambda = 1 - D k^2 + i v.k + ..., with D > 0 unless the weights are degenerate. Expectation: no waves; diffusion is forced by positivity. A counterexample is a HIT. DELIVERABLE in your unit worktree: probes/work/compute/dispersion-under-positive-weights/<your worker name>/run.py (self-contained; exact arithmetic wherever the statement is exact; numpy only for the numerical cross-checks named) and RESULT.md (the table or formulas, in plain text). run.py prints one line per result, a final `SUMMARY: <the main result in one line>`, and `HIT: <what>` ONLY if a result contradicts the expectation stated in the task (that is the interesting case: report it precisely). Two workers do each computation independently; the supervisor compares them.
